text: This is the agency's lead list. A new one just came in from S-GE... Kestrelyn, a Finnish company with a glucose and lactate patch for women in endurance sport.
I paste their one pager in, just as it arrived, and ask for the needs.

Apertus finds seven needs, each tied to the sentence it came from. The main one is a clinical study with women who have type 1 diabetes. And the revenue and valuation were struck on this machine, before anything went out.

Then it searches about three thousand pages from the University, ARTORG and the Diabetes Center. Two open models do the ranking, right here on this machine... BGE-M3 finds pages by meaning, and the BGE reranker, v2 M3, puts them in order.
Every match comes with the quotes it was found on, how well Bern covers the need, and the unit behind it. Cleanroom capacity has no evidence at all, so it says no match instead of guessing.
I accept the ones I'd put in front of their CEO.
The evidence map traces every claim back. This one, on the menstrual cycle, is quoted word for word from the Diabetes Center's own page.
Next, the pitch. First it pulls out the facts, each with its quote.
Only checked facts go into the brief, so I compare every card with its source and tick it.
Once they're all ticked, Apertus writes the pitch from those facts, and nothing else.
I export a clean PDF for the CEO, and the lead waits for their reply.
When the CEO says yes, it drafts an email to each research group, from the pitch the CEO actually read.
Across all leads, the capability map shows where Bern is strong, where it's thin... and where it has nothing yet.
And the pipeline shows every lead, from new to won.
If a gap is really a site we haven't read yet, adding it is one step. Public pages only.
Or skip all of that. Drop the company's PDF on Bärner Mutz, and the pitch gets drafted.
Every card is still traced to its quote, and the officer still ticks each one before the PDF goes out.
And if the CEO reads German, just ask.
